sections.html:
About 35,000 people live in Randolph, a suburban city south of Boston that borders Quincy on the north and lies in Norfolk County. Its 2020 census count came to 34,984. The land has very little water, about 4 percent of the area, and sits at an elevation of about 184 feet. The Cochato River and the Blue Hill River drain the town into the Neponset River.

Randolph has a city form of government but kept "Town of Randolph" as its official name, one of thirteen Massachusetts municipalities that did so. Expect to see both forms on documents, and use whichever one your attorney and the deed use.

sections.h2: Why many houses are the same age
sections.html:
Braintree let Randolph go as a separate town in 1793, naming it for Peyton Randolph of the Continental Congress. Shoes and boots were the trade, and by 1850 Randolph was one of the nation's leading boot producers. When the trade faded in the early 1900s, the town became a residential community.

Population nearly tripled in two decades, which means a big portion of the housing was built in a short window. Houses of similar age may need roofs, boilers and windows replaced around the same time. You can look up your own house's age on the assessor's property card.

Randolph sits at a crossroads of major routes, which helps with commuters.

  • Interstate 93 and U.S. Route 1
  • Massachusetts Route 24, the Fall River Expressway
  • Route 28 and Route 139

Rail service comes from the Holbrook/Randolph station on the MBTA Commuter Rail's Fall River/New Bedford Line, and bus service is run by the MBTA and the Brockton Area Transit Authority.

When you describe your house, give the drive time to the highway ramps and the rail station. For commuters, that detail often counts as much as the kitchen.

A council-manager government began in 2010 under the 2009 charter. Earlier, the town ran on a representative town meeting that was adopted in 1947 and took effect in 1949.

For assessment questions, visit the Board of Assessors at Town Hall, 41 South Main Street, Randolph, MA 02368. The assessors page shows that the board meets on the first Thursday of each month at 5:15 p.m. in the Washington Room. Call ahead or check the page for the current meeting schedule before you go.

Think your house is valued too high? An abatement lowers the tax bill if you can prove the fair cash value is under the assessed figure. The steps come from state law and are laid out in the Appellate Tax Board's guide.

  • Keep every installment current, since a late payment can forfeit the appeal.
  • Submit the state's abatement form to the assessors before the first installment due date printed on your bill.
  • Three months is the assessors' window to decide. Silence counts as a denial.
  • After that you get three more months to take the case to the Appellate Tax Board.

Values are measured as of January 1 before the fiscal year. Sales of similar houses nearby are the strongest evidence, so gather those and photographs. Read the Appellate Tax Board guide before you file.

Your deed goes on record at the Norfolk Registry of Deeds, because Randolph lies in Norfolk County. Nearly every sale involves three items.

  • Fire department certificate. You must show that the smoke and carbon monoxide alarms meet sale standards. The Randolph fire department does the inspection and charges a fee.
  • Deed excise. The registry collects $2.28 per $500 of consideration at recording, paid by attorney's or bank check.
  • Recording fee. The registry charges $156.00 to record a deed on recorded land.

Your attorney will confirm the exact excise and who pays it under your contract. More detail is on the Mass.gov alarm inspection page and the Norfolk Registry fee schedule.

The nearest weather record, at Blue Hill, shows 53.86 inches of precipitation and 69.7 inches of snow in an average year, with January lows averaging 18.3 degrees Fahrenheit. The record low is minus 21 degrees and the record high is 101. Houses here carry a real heating load in winter and real humidity in summer, so buyers check insulation, the furnace and the roof.

Because two rivers drain the town, ask the town and your insurer whether your lot has any flood exposure, and write down anything you know about wet basements before a buyer asks.

sections.h2: What to do before you call a buyer
sections.html:
Check your house's age on the assessor's property card, then walk through it with the roof, boiler and windows in mind. Houses built in the same postwar wave tend to need the same big-ticket work together, so a buyer's inspector will probably find it.

Gather the deed, your latest tax bill and notes on any water in the basement. Call the Randolph fire department to learn what the alarm inspection involves and what it costs. If the property is part of an estate, bring the paperwork that shows who can sign. A tidy folder lets your attorney move quickly, and it lets a cash buyer such as Cash Home Buyers make an offer on the house in its present condition without a long back and forth.

There are three ways to sell: with an agent, by yourself or to a cash buyer. Each one swaps time and effort for price and certainty in a different way.

  • Listing: reaches the most buyers, but brings showings, repair requests after an inspection and a financing contingency.
  • Selling on your own: saves a commission, yet you do the marketing, paperwork and buyer screening.
  • Cash sale: closes faster and more simply, though the price can land below a fully prepared listing.

With so many Randolph houses of the same era, a house that has not been updated may compete against freshly renovated ones. That gap is where an as-is sale tends to make sense. Whichever you choose, the fire certificate, the recorded deed and the registry fees stay on your checklist.

faqs.q: What county is Randolph, MA in?
faqs.a: Norfolk County. Your deed is recorded at its registry.

faqs.q: Is Randolph a town or a city?
faqs.a: Sort of both. A city charter with a council-manager government took effect in January 2010, yet the official name is still "Town of Randolph."

faqs.q: Who do I call about my Randolph property assessment?
faqs.a: Start with the Board of Assessors at Town Hall, 41 South Main Street, which meets on the first Thursday of each month at 5:15 p.m.

faqs.q: Do I need a smoke and CO certificate to sell in Randolph?
faqs.a: Yes. The local fire department has to certify that your alarms meet sale standards.

faqs.q: How much is the Norfolk County deed excise tax?
faqs.a: The registry charges $2.28 on every $500 of the stated price.
